definitions.meaning: an instant is a moment, a very brief stretch of time
to support a motion or a candidate is to back it formally

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a brief moment of time, and the verb meaning to back a proposal.

indicators.note: the first word takes the second into itself, as a family adopts a child

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A theatre takes on a different place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: accommodation in the sense of space for keeping goods.

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
wed means got married

explanation.surface: An intimidated officer tied the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: intimidated or made timid by bullying.

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down entry the short word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A pub table game is knocked over during an evening on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses ON to NO; 'out' rearranges NIGHT to THING. Bagatelle is also a pub game, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bagatelle is a trifle, something of no importance.

definitions.meaning: British slang for beer or alcoholic drink generally

explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is informal British English for beer, as well as for a hard hit.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for alcoholic drink, and an everyday word for a heavy punch or blow.

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange
a mate is a pal; the 's is a link
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A keen cook agreed to use a friend's upmarket recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a non-professional who does something purely for love of it.

clue.text: Female metalworker relieved in South Africa

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a smith works metal

explanation.surface: A woman blacksmith feels relief while working in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladysmith is a town in Natal, South Africa, famously besieged and relieved in the Boer War (1900).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the South African town whose siege was lifted by British forces in 1900.

clue.text: Zionist leader leaves Cornish town as act of atonement

indicators.note: the letter departs from the town name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Zionist figure departs a seaside town to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: self-punishment undertaken to make amends for wrongdoing.

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A stylish party climbs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mount is to climb or go up.

clue.text: Lacking reputation despite anything to the contrary

parts.note: lacking something is being not with it, split as two words
one's standing is one's status or reputation

explanation.surface: Someone without a good name carries on regardless of objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal word meaning in spite of whatever might be said against it.

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A political figure enjoyed a gin-based mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the leader of the Indian independence movement against British rule.

parts.note: betting odds of one to one are called evens
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler backs a horse at even money and gets a decent return.
explanation.walkthrough: The betting surface hides a church word: 'service' is a religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Anglican evening prayer service is a kind of church service.

clue.text: Called into action, when out to lunch

indicators.note: one word placed into another, so the telephoned word goes inside the deed

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
rang is the past tense of ring, to call by phone

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned to work at the very moment they had gone for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' is an idiom meaning crazy, not away eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being out to lunch means being mad or not in one's right mind.

clue.text: Two masters introduced to change their own college

indicators.note: the pair is put into the other word

parts.note: alter means change
MA is a Master of Arts; two of them make the pair
the second MA of the pair

explanation.surface: Two graduates try to reform their own former university.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person's old school or university is called this, Latin for nourishing mother.

parts.note: Romeo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: Romeo felt unwell after being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complaining bitterly or scolding someone is to have spoken out against them harshly.

parts.note: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: An opera heroine walks away calm and balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a psychologically balanced, ordinary person is described as being so.

clue.text: Zero? Less than zero? About zero? That's unpromising!

parts.note: O looks like zero

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a number less than zero is minus
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A gloomy assessment of a score that keeps getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: threatening or suggesting that things will go badly.

parts.note: to let is to allow or tolerate
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Putting up with a drink that turns out to be poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an anticlimax or something that fails to meet expectations.

clue.text: Look for the men of Smithfield

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang a look is a ..., short for ... hook
Smithfield is London's historic meat market, staffed by meat traders

explanation.surface: Someone searches for workers at a London meat market.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look, so 'have a butcher's' means have a look. Smithfield is London's meat market.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a glance, and plural for meat traders who cut and sell carcasses.

definitions.meaning: a joke reading: a plot of ground, a bed, along a counter or bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'counterplot' looks like a scheme; read it as a garden plot (bed) at a pub counter (bar).
explanation.definitionFit: A wounding remark is described as pointed; the second reading jokes about a flowerbed at a counter.

clue.text: Sauce bachelor's put in Mexican food

indicators.note: the degree letters are put inside the food

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla
BA's, a Bachelor of Arts degree, gives these letters

explanation.surface: A graduate adds a hot sauce to a taco.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brand of fiery chilli pepper condiment.

clue.text: Chatterbox loses head when seeing snake

indicators.note: the word sheds its first letter

parts.note: a prattler talks constantly

explanation.surface: A gossip panics on spotting a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rattlesnake, informally called by this shortened name.

clue.text: Put off drinking? I am showing calibre!

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the other, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from alcohol boasts of their quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calibre' here is the bore width of a gun barrel, not quality of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the calibre of a gun is the internal width measurement of its barrel.

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it, as a trap holds an animal

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
a rat is a common pest

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a pest-control worker who is catching rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scold or tell someone off angrily.

clue.text: Get to deliver a sermon, but not quietly

indicators.note: the letter is excluded from the longer word

parts.note: to preach is to give a sermon
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A vicar manages to give a sermon, though loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to arrive at a place or achieve a target.

clue.text: Cover trials only, perhaps, in a contentious way

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A suggestion that only trials be reported, which would cause arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done in a manner provoking dispute or argument.

clue.text: Wrinkled, being submerged about an hour

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: sunk means having gone under the water

explanation.surface: Fingers go wrinkly after an hour in the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: something that has contracted or shrivelled, as skin wrinkles when it does.

indicators.note: one letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a brother is a male relative
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A family member flees from difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fuss, nuisance or inconvenience.
